clue.text: Mine closes branch that's a bad place to be

indicators.note: the mine comes at the close, after the branch, in the answer

parts.note: an arm is a branch, as of a river or an organisation
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A miner's warning that a certain branch tunnel is a dangerous spot to stand in.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally an armpit is a squalid, unpleasant place, as in 'the armpit of the world'.

clue.text: One who makes good dryer introduced by salesman

indicators.note: the salesman comes first, leading in the dryer that follows

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
an airer is a frame for drying clothes

explanation.surface: A tumble dryer is brought in by the salesman who sold it, now acting as the fixer.
explanation.definitionFit: To make good is to mend, so the person who fixes things is a repairer.

clue.text: Things appropriate to youth at the outset

parts.note: proper means appropriate or fitting

indicators.note: the opening letters of the words to and youth are taken

explanation.surface: Possessions considered fit for a young person to have from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Property is one's possessions or belongings, the stuff one owns.

clue.text: Kid at home prepared for light work

indicators.note: the letters are made ready in a new arrangement, prepared like a dish

explanation.surface: A child at home has got ready a little easy task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light work' sounds like an easy chore; here it is light opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado is a comic operetta by Gilbert and Sullivan, a work of light opera.

clue.text: Home before time, wound up fiancé

indicators.note: home comes before the rest in the answer

parts.note: in means at home
wound up means finished, ended

explanation.surface: Home before the deadline, the fiancé has ended up there.
explanation.definitionFit: One's intended is the person one is engaged to marry.

clue.text: Finally visiting the town we holidayed in most recently?

definitions.meaning: the idiom means as a last option, finally

definitions.text: visiting the town we holidayed in most recently?
definitions.meaning: read literally: being in the latest holiday resort we went to

explanation.surface: Eventually going back to the seaside town of our latest holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means when all else has failed, i.e. ultimately; literally it places one in the most recent resort.

clue.text: Physical amount of energy left over in New York

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: the turned word sits inside the abbreviation
in a down entry, over means the word is turned back

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A physics remark about how much energy remains unused in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reads 'left' backwards, a down-clue convention; 'in' signals the container. 'Physical amount' is a quantity in physics, not a bodily one.
explanation.definitionFit: Entropy is a quantity in thermodynamics measuring disorder, a physical amount.

clue.text: Note downpour develop over time and where it ends up

parts.note: D is a musical note
rain is a downpour
to age is to develop or mature over time

explanation.surface: A remark that a heavy shower matures and finally finds where it goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainwater runs off into drains, so drainage is its final destination.

clue.text: Classic TV series — key dramas broadcast over years

parts.note: D is a musical key

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A vintage television show whose principal plays have been aired over many years.
explanation.definitionFit: Dad's Army is a classic BBC sitcom about the Home Guard in wartime Britain.

clue.text: Player against work with piano nonet being composed

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

indicators.note: the letters are arranged like music being composed

explanation.surface: A musician competing with a piano nonet as a new work is composed.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent is an adversary, someone who plays against you in a game.

clue.text: Maroon thread

explanation.surface: A dark red-brown sewing thread.
explanation.definitionFit: To strand is to leave someone helpless, as castaways are marooned; a strand is also a single thread.

clue.text: Just the same as Ernie, perhaps

parts.note: like can mean as, in the manner of
Ernie Wise was the partner of Eric Morecambe in the British comedy double act

explanation.surface: Exactly the same as someone called Ernie, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernie Wise was half of Morecambe and Wise, a famous British comedy double act.
explanation.definitionFit: Likewise means in the same way, similarly.

clue.text: A home to weep over in Balkan country

indicators.note: over means the whole string is turned around

parts.note: in means at home
to sob is to weep

explanation.surface: Somewhere to come home and cry in a Balkan land.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosnia is a country of the Balkan peninsula in south-east Europe.

clue.text: Note a carrier with more than one iron canister of gunpowder?

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

parts.words: carrier with more than one iron
parts.note: a golf caddy carries a bag of several iron clubs

explanation.surface: Musical note on a bearer with several irons, and a container of explosive powder.
explanation.walkthrough: Gunpowder is a kind of green tea with leaves rolled into pellets, not the explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea caddy is a small tin for storing tea leaves, such as gunpowder tea.

clue.text: A lot discounted spiteful gossip over Charlie and Rick

parts.note: dirt is scandal or malicious gossip
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a rick is a stack, a heap

explanation.surface: Plenty of nasty gossip about two men, Charlie and Rick, being marked down.
explanation.walkthrough: Rick is not a name here but a stack, as in a hayrick.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dirt cheap has been reduced in price enormously, very inexpensive indeed.

clue.text: Attempt to introduce the second of horses here?

indicators.note: the try takes the picked letter into its middle

parts.note: a try is an attempt

indicators.note: the second letter of the word horses is used

explanation.surface: Trying to bring in horses, with a question about where.
explanation.walkthrough: The wooden horse was introduced into Troy, making the 'here?' an apt definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Troy is the city into which the Greeks smuggled soldiers inside a wooden horse.

clue.text: Devious few do act false

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Few people behave deceitfully, yet those few do act falsely.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-faced person is insincere and deceitful, showing a different face to different people.

clue.text: What elevates the way religious festival gets swapped around

indicators.note: the two halves of the festival's name change places

parts.note: Passover is the Jewish spring festival

explanation.surface: A religious holiday is moved around and that lifts the road.
explanation.definitionFit: An overpass is a bridge carrying a road over another road, raising the route.

clue.text: Depend — only without me

indicators.note: without means the following word is left out

parts.note: merely means only

explanation.surface: Someone told they can lean on others alone without the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: To rely on something is to depend on it.

clue.text: Editor is embarrassed luvvy?

parts.note: red is the colour of embarrassment
luvvy is British slang for a gushing theatrical person, often an actor

explanation.surface: Asking whether an editor is a self-conscious showbiz type.
explanation.walkthrough: A luvvy is British slang for an effusive actor or theatre person.
explanation.definitionFit: A redactor is one who edits or prepares text for publication.

clue.text: Lake supporting fish which may be close to the bottom?

definitions.text: which may be close to the bottom?

indicators.note: in a down entry, the lake goes below the fish, holding it up

parts.note: the ling is an edible sea fish
Lake Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A lake holds up a fish that may lurk near the bed of the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The bottom is a person's backside, not the lake bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is underwear, worn right next to one's behind.

clue.text: Roll in once drunk for work

indicators.note: the roll goes inside the jumbled letters
drunk means unsteady, so the letters are shaken up

parts.note: to roll over is to turn

explanation.surface: Tumbling about once intoxicated, on the way to the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles the word once, and 'in' sets the synonym for roll inside it. 'Work' is a piece of music, not a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturne is a piece of music, a dreamy night-piece such as Chopin's.

clue.text: Establishment making good bed covers?

parts.note: sounds like an upholsterer, but the beds are nail beds and their covers are the nails a salon tidies

explanation.surface: A shop that repairs bedspreads.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail salon treats the hard plates that cover the nail beds of fingers.

clue.text: Prohibit going either way in crossing

indicators.note: the short word goes inside the crossing

parts.note: a ford is a river crossing
bi is short for bisexual, attracted either way

explanation.surface: A sign banning traffic in both directions across a junction.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbid is to ban or prohibit.

clue.text: Swap over shillings or sixpences, say

parts.note: ex means former, over and done with
small coins are change; shillings and sixpences were old British coins

explanation.surface: Trading in old shillings or sixpences for something else.
explanation.walkthrough: Shillings and sixpences were small coins in pre-decimal British money.
explanation.definitionFit: An exchange is a swap, a giving of one thing for another.

clue.text: Mostly ill-tempered English poet

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter is used

parts.note: crabby means grumpy, ill-tempered

explanation.surface: A grumpy English poet, more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: George Crabbe was an English poet of the late 18th and early 19th centuries.

clue.text: Exhaust patent anger

parts.note: patent means obvious, overt
ire means anger

explanation.surface: Wearing out obvious rage, or a car exhaust patent causing fury.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtire is to tire out too much, to exhaust.

clue.text: Not all there is to see in fourth rate feature

indicators.note: the short word is to be found inside the other pieces

parts.note: D is the fourth grade, after A, B and C
a trait is a feature

explanation.surface: A deficient feature in a fourth-rate thing, which is not complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Distrait means absent-minded or distracted, mentally elsewhere.

clue.text: Origins of Pooh, Owl, Roo, Kanga, Eeyore, Rabbit and Piglet

indicators.note: the first letters of the six Winnie-the-Pooh names are taken

explanation.surface: A roll call of the Winnie-the-Pooh animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Piglet is a playful definition: a porker is a pig being fattened, and Piglet is one of the gang.
explanation.definitionFit: A porker is a young pig fattened for its meat, and Piglet is a little pig.
